environment: Owner Mac Studio local Ubuntu24 ARM64 VM; no GitHub/cloud execution
implementation: One bounded feedback endpoint per actual RouterHandle allocation, cleared by owned cleanup. No packet buffers, idle policy readers, global source registry or detached feedback tasks.
Actual successful video ingress records a publisher SSRC and weak generation predicate. Actual successful guarded egress records the emitted receiver SSRC and current Core route epoch.

Receiver feedback must match its physical handle, emitted SSRC and route epoch. Core reacquires both current permissions and resolves the selected publisher port; the adapter downcasts that exact allocation and checks its current source SSRC and binding.

Publisher dispatch rewrites to its own actual handle, SSRC, activation epoch and independent sequence. Shared publisher100ms coalescing bounds fan-in in addition to per-route bounds; uncertain local send consumes its sequence.

Canonical reader separates bounded checked video feedback from clock/media. Native negotiation defaults disabled and does not advertise the profile. An installed profile must admit an authenticated epoch notice before feedback can use its record.
remaining: The new canonical QUIC cases use controlled readiness and epoch-notice admission. They do not prove signed Service epoch negotiation or decoded media.

Production NativeNegotiation still uses the default-disabled profile. Implement explicit capability negotiation, signed original-operation/physical-incarnation/generation/selected-source association, monotonic notice ordering and first admitted/submitted packet boundary before enabling it.
Wire feedback into Node and Rust live source workers, with original frame clock and bounded force-keyframe handling; prove receiver startup and fragment-loss recovery.
